sources.title: Liviu I. Nicolaescu, An Invitation to Morse Theory, second edition
sources.locator: Full PDF table of contents, printed p. iii / PDF p. 2, lists Chapter 2 §2.4 `Morse–Smale Dynamics` at printed p. 53. Read the whole §2.4, printed pp. 53–61 / PDF pp. 62–70, from its heading through Corollary 2.4.14; the next heading §2.5 starts at printed p. 62.

contents.name: Stable and unstable sets W⁻ and W⁺ (paragraph following Lemma 2.4.1)
Remark 2.4.4.
contents.reason: The singular topology of closures of stable and unstable manifolds needs a stratification or compactification theory; this trajectory-foundation page proves neither and does not use the claim.

contents.name: Theorem 2.4.5.
contents.reason: This is the existence of a transverse Morse–Smale gradient-like field, the dedicated genericity and transversality theorem of DT-4 rather than an assumption or conclusion of DT-3.

contents.name: Lemma 2.4.6 (The main deformation lemma).
contents.reason: Its prescribed perturbation of a field inside a regular band is the relative perturbation mechanism needed for the Morse–Smale construction on DT-4, not for defining ordinary trajectories.

contents.name: Lemma 2.4.7 (The moving lemma).
contents.reason: The ambient-isotopy transversality move supplies the DT-4 Morse–Smale perturbation theorem and is not a prerequisite for the elementary flow and endpoint facts established here.

contents.name: Definition 2.4.8.
contents.reason: The definition of a Morse–Smale pair requires the transverse intersections whose statement and consequences are deliberately introduced on DT-4.

contents.name: Remark 2.4.9.
contents.reason: The no-nonpositive-index-drop conclusion uses Morse–Smale transversality and becomes the DT-4 corollary about its parametrized and unparametrized trajectory spaces.

contents.name: Definition 2.4.10.
contents.reason: Self-indexing is a critical-value rearrangement convention used for index-filtered handle decompositions, which are constructed only after the DT-5 handle-attachment theorem.

contents.name: Theorem 2.4.11 (Smale).
contents.reason: Existence of self-indexing Morse–Smale data joins the later rearrangement and transversality developments, while DT-3 only fixes the underlying descending-flow conventions.

contents.name: Lemma 2.4.12 (Rearrangement lemma).
contents.reason: Changing critical values while preserving a gradient-like field is precisely the later critical-value interchange move for handle decompositions.

contents.name: Remark 2.4.13.
contents.reason: Its clock-modifier interpretation and multi-critical-point extension explain the rearrangement lemma, so they travel with that later construction rather than being an unsupported aside here.

contents.name: Corollary 2.4.14.
contents.reason: The corollary packages self-indexing together with preservation of Morse–Smale data and is the exact input to the later handle-ordering and self-indexing page.

contents.name: Theorem 2.4.15.
contents.reason: The Heegaard-decomposition application is specific to compact connected three-manifolds and would require handlebody theory beyond this general trajectory and gradient-like-field foundation.

contents.name: Remark following Lemma 13.1 (the two norm-square formulas)
Definition 13.1.
contents.reason: Height reparameterizations give the same unparametrized curves with a different vector field, but this page fixes ordinary negative-gradient time and does not yet construct quotient trajectory spaces.

contents.name: Lemma 13.3.
contents.reason: The normalized vector field with df/dt=1 is a regular-level slicing tool, and DT-4 uses such slices to identify unparametrized Morse trajectory spaces.

contents.name: Proposition 13.5.
contents.reason: The partition of a compact manifold by unstable cells is used to connect trajectories to its handle and CW-type decomposition, which begins only after the DT-4 prerequisites are complete.

contents.name: Tilted-torus discussion and Figure 13.5
contents.reason: The perturbation that separates the symmetric torus flow is an explicit Morse–Smale example, so its transverse-separatrix analysis belongs to the companion examples for DT-4.

contents.name: 13.3 `The Morse–Smale condition` (opening heading)
contents.reason: The exact read range stops before this next section; its transverse-intersection definition and genericity results are planned as the substantive content of DT-4.

canonical.name: All trajectories and stable/unstable sets use the descending equation γ˙=−grad_g f (or the descending flow of a downward gradient-like field). With this convention Wᵘ has dimension index(p) and Wˢ has dimension n−index(p).

A downward gradient-like field is required to agree with the standard negative linear model in Morse coordinates near every critical point; df(X)<0 away from critical points alone is not an adequate replacement.
Compactness has three distinct jobs: it makes a smooth field complete, supplies nonempty tail limit sets, and makes the isolated critical set finite so each connected limit set is a point.

The local stable-manifold statement is only a coordinate disk statement. The global Euclidean conclusion is obtained separately by flow exhaustion and is deliberately stated for immersed, not embedded, submanifolds.
On a noncompact manifold, the proper-slab proposition is a conditional nonescape result; it must not be read as an assertion that every gradient or gradient-like vector field is complete.
